legend: Lavender is too lazy to come up with a good problem, so he will recycle one from two years ago!

Given an array a%%ZSMJ0%% of n%%ZSMJ1%% integers. Initially, you can choose a number s%%ZSMJ2%%, and mark the s-th element as used. Then, you need to perform the following operation n−1%%ZSMJ3%% times:

On the x%%ZSMJ4%%-th operation, choose two numbers u%%ZSMJ5%% and v%%ZSMJ6%% such that the u%%ZSMJ7%%-th element is used, the v%%ZSMJ8%%-th element is not used, and |au−av|%%ZSMJ9%% is divisible by x%%ZSMJ10%%.
Mark the v%%ZSMJ11%%-th element as used.
You have to determine if it is possible to perform all n−1%%ZSMJ12%% operations. If so, output any valid operation sequence.
input: Each test consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains an integer t (1≤t≤100%%ZSMJ13%%) — the number of test cases. Then follows the description of the test cases.
The first line of each test case contains the number n (2≤n≤2000%%ZSMJ14%%) — the number of elements in the array.
The second line of each test case contains n numbers a1,a2,…an%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤ai≤109%%ZSMJ16%%).
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ17%% over all test cases does not exceed 2000%%ZSMJ18%%.
output: For each test case, if there is no solution, then output "NO" (without quotes).

Otherwise, output "YES" (without quotes), and then output a number s%%ZSMJ19%% on the first line, denoting the first used element. In the next n−1%%ZSMJ20%% lines, output the numbers ui%%ZSMJ21%% and vi%%ZSMJ22%% (u≠v%%ZSMJ23%%), denoting the two chosen number for operation i%%ZSMJ24%%.
note: In the first testcase, you can also choose s=2%%ZSMJ25%%, u1=2%%ZSMJ26%%, and v1=1%%ZSMJ27%%.
